summary.headline: A good, cash-rich cable maker, but at Rs 97.80 the price is about 2.6 times fair value on the standard 22% required return
summary.text: ACL Cables PLC (ACL.N0000), Sri Lanka's largest cable maker, is a good business: return on equity of about 18% (18.4% in 2025/26), no loss in ten years and Rs 13.4bn of unit trusts and deposits against Rs 5.1bn of borrowings. This is a full rebuild from the 2025/26 annual report and the September 2026 interim in the site's current format: printed figures only, every method computed by code, and new management and shareholder sections. The figures haven't changed since 17 November: six-month EPS Rs 4.61 (Rs 4.30), twelve-month EPS Rs 9.13, but the September quarter was flat (EPS Rs 2.04 against Rs 2.06) as the gross margin slipped to 23.8% and a Rs 144mn exchange loss hit. Copper stock still ties up cash: inventory Rs 19.1bn (Rs 14.1bn in March), operating cash flow minus Rs 4.66bn for the half, paid for by cashing Rs 2.8bn of unit trusts and Rs 2.5bn of new short-term loans. At a 22.0% cost of equity (beta 1.34, provisional) an 17–18% return on equity is worth a little under book value, so the four methods put fair value at about Rs 37.60 (Rs 39.10 on 17 November; the small fall is the code's residual income method and the new treatment of minorities, not the business). At Rs 97.80 the share is 10.7x twelve-month earnings and 1.76x NAV of Rs 55.46. I'd buy at up to about Rs 32.00 and treat under Rs 28.20 as a strong buy. The business still passes 3 of 4 tests, so it stays on the watch list.

quality.reason: High returns, net cash and an unbroken profit record; still weak at turning profit into cash and dividends.

tests.label: Return on equity of 15% or more
tests.note: Profit to owners over average owners' equity: 17.8% over the twelve months to September 2026 (company's own 2025/26 ratio 18.4%). About 21% on average over five years, from 11% in 2023/24 to 29% in 2022/23. Diluted by the investment pile.

tests.label: Net debt no more than equity

tests.label: Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: But profit swings with copper prices (down 49% in 2023/24), 2025/26 included a Rs 0.70bn property revaluation gain, and exchange gains and losses move single quarters by Rs 150–600mn.

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends
tests.note: Operating cash flow was minus Rs 4.66bn in April–September 2026 against Rs 3.88bn of profit (Rs 1.43bn against Rs 7.28bn in 2025/26); dividends about 7% of profit.

methodReadings.reading: The price is 1.76x NAV; about Rs 14.50 of NAV is net cash and investments and Rs 3.50 is investment property.
About 21% on average over five years, from 11% (2023/24) to 29% (2022/23). Good, but below the 22% required return, which is why value comes out under book.
On twelve-month EPS Rs 9.13. The forward P/E justified at a 22% cost of equity is about 4x; the ten-year year-end average was about 5.9x.
Rs 0.60 a share is about 7% of profit; cash after maintenance capex covered 2025/26 dividends about 3 times, so the dividend is safe but small.
Operating business Rs 30.70 a share at a 21.3% WACC, plus Rs 15.50 of investments less minorities. 58% of the DCF value comes after year 5.
A real cushion, but copper stock and receivables swallowed about Rs 4.4bn of it in six months.

models.name: Whole-company DCF plus investments, less minorities
models.comment: Whole-company DCF: cash before interest after maintenance capex Rs 5.0 / 5.9 / 5.9bn (trailing operating profit Rs 9.20bn less the one-off Rs 0.70bn property gain, × (1 − 30.8%); bear 15% lower, about the 2024/25 level), growing 4% / 8% / 11% for five years, then 4% / 5% / 6%, less the reinvestment that growth needs at a 12% / 16% / 20% return on new capital, at WACC 22.7% / 21.3% / 19.9%, less net debt Rs 3.0bn: Rs 21.61 / 30.74 / 40.40 a share. Plus Rs 15.49 a share of unit trusts, deposits, investment property, associates and FVOCI shares less minorities at book (30 Sep 2026). Value after year 5: 44% / 58% / 67%, under the 75% flag. The DCF starts from operating profit, not one year's cash flow, because copper stock swings cash flow (Rs 1.4bn in 2025/26, minus Rs 4.7bn in the last six months).

models.name: P/E method
models.comment: EPS for the year to March 2027 of Rs 7.60 / 9.10 / 10.30 (six months so far Rs 4.61, so a second half of Rs 2.99 / 4.49 / 5.69 against Rs 4.52 a year earlier) × 3.7 / 4.2 / 4.8, the forward P/E justified at the cost of equity when growth is paid for (payout = 1 − growth ÷ ROE, ROE 14% / 17% / 20%). Base EPS equals the Rs 9.13 run-rate; the bear (17% below) assumes copper prices fall and stock loses value, as in 2023/24.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: NAV Rs 55.46 × (long-run ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth): ROE 14% / 17% / 20%, growth 4% / 5% / 6%, cost of equity 23.5% / 22.0% / 20.5%.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Book value Rs 55.46 (September 2026); ROE moving from 17.8% (twelve months) to 14% / 17% / 20% over ten years; 8% payout throughout; after year ten the excess return grows at 4% / 5% / 6%, at a 23.5% / 22.0% / 20.5% cost of equity. Because ROE stays below the cost of equity, keeping 92% of profit lowers value per rupee kept. Lower than the Rs 34.13 of 17 November, whose hand calculation raised the payout after year 5.

modelsNote: ACL is a steady earner over a cycle but its yearly cash flow swings with copper stock, so the DCF starts from after-tax operating profit and charges growth ÷ return on capital as reinvestment each year. Its unit trusts, deposits and other investments, less the minorities' book equity, are added as a separate piece, so the DCF method is a sum of the parts. It pays out about 7% of profit, so a dividend model would say little. Growth check: assumed 4% / 8% / 11% for five years against 14.5% supported by 2025/26 reinvestment (68.8% of after-tax operating profit) × return on capital (21.1%), all within. The supported figure is flattered: almost all reinvestment was stock and receivables as copper prices rose (price, not volume); profit kept × ROE gives 15.3%. P/E, P/B and residual income use the 22.0% cost of equity; the DCF uses WACC 21.3%.

assumptions.label: Cash before interest after maintenance capex, start

scenarios.common: Required return from CAPM with a country premium: risk-free 8.24% (12.24% bond less 4.0% default spread), mature premium 4.2% plus country premium 6.08%, beta 1.34 (provisional). Tax 30.8% (2025/26 effective). Net debt Rs 3.0bn (borrowings and leases less cash, 30 Sep 2026); unit trusts, deposits, investment property, associates and FVOCI shares less minorities add Rs 15.49 a share. Long-run reinvestment = growth ÷ return on capital (4/12 = 33%, 5/16 = 31%, 6/20 = 30%). Payout 8%. Book value Rs 55.46; 718.72mn shares.

sensitivity.title: Residual income, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Starting ROE 17.8%, growth 5%, payout 8%. Even a 20% long-run ROE at a 20.5% cost of equity gives under Rs 50; Rs 97.80 needs a much lower required return with ROE staying near 20%.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 16,561 in total, against Rs 48,900 at Rs 97.80.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 32.00 needs about a 67% fall from Rs 97.80. This year the share has traded between Rs 81.00 and Rs 107.75. Allowing for the 1-for-3 split it was about Rs 41 in March 2025 and Rs 28 in March 2024, so these prices are only two years old, but getting back there would need a copper slump or a market-wide sell-off. Realistically this is a share to watch, not to buy, unless the required return falls (lower bond yields or country risk) or the price drops sharply.

higher: A lower required return: rupee bond yields or Sri Lanka's default spread falling, or a verified local 5-year beta well below 1.34.
Copper prices staying high without hurting demand, and exports keeping up 40%+ growth.
The gross margin recovering towards 27–28% and stock falling back, releasing cash.
A much bigger dividend, or using the cash pile for a well-priced expansion.
ROE staying above 20% without help from exchange gains or property revaluations.
lower: Copper prices falling, so stock bought at high prices loses value (as in 2023/24).
Less spending on power lines and construction (the CEB buys over 20% of group sales).
Short-term loans keep rising to carry stock (Rs 4.4bn now).
The rupee strengthening, turning exchange gains into losses (as in July–September).
Bond yields rising again, lifting the required return.

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the annual reports to March 2025 and March 2026 and the interim reports to September 2026. Per-share figures before 2025/26 have been divided by three for the share split. The beta is provisional (web-search stand-in for Damodaran's data). The price is the CSE close on 17 November 2026; check it live. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

fullText:
**ACL Cables PLC (ACL.N0000): full rebuild, 21 November 2026**

**Summary.** A good business at a price well above fair value. Fair value about Rs 37.60 a share (Rs 39.10 on 17 November); buy at up to Rs 32.00, strong buy under Rs 28.20. At Rs 97.80 (CSE close, 20 November 2026) the share is 1.76x NAV and 10.7x twelve-month earnings. Category: watch list (3 of 4 business tests passed, price above the buy price), unchanged.

**What changed.** No new figures: this is a rebuild of the 17 November analysis from the same two reports (the 2025/26 annual report and the interim to 30 September 2026) in the site's current format. The research record now holds only printed figures with their pages, the interim's comparative columns are their own periods, and code works out the twelve-month figures, ROE, net debt and tax rate. All four methods are now computed by scripts/valuation.py, which moved fair value down 4%:
- Minorities (about 14% of equity, in Kelani Cables, ACL Plastics and Cable Solutions) are now subtracted at book value, Damodaran's way, rather than multiplying everything by 86%.
- Unit trusts and deposits are now added to the DCF as separate pieces rather than netted against debt, so WACC is 21.3% (22.0% before).
- Residual income holds the 8% payout for all ten years (Rs 29.13, against Rs 34.13 when the payout was raised after year 5 by hand).

**Latest results (six months to 30 September 2026, unaudited).** Revenue Rs 25.79bn (up 22%; exports Rs 6.23bn, up 46%). Gross margin 24.0% (28.0%). Profit to owners Rs 3.31bn (up 7%), EPS Rs 4.61 (Rs 4.30). The September quarter alone: revenue up 26% to Rs 14.30bn, EPS Rs 2.04 (Rs 2.06), with a Rs 144mn exchange loss. Inventory Rs 19.08bn (Rs 14.13bn in March); operating cash flow minus Rs 4.66bn, funded by cashing Rs 2.84bn of unit trusts and Rs 2.5bn of new short-term loans. NAV Rs 55.46.

**Required return.** Cost of equity 22.0% = 8.24% + 1.34 × (4.2% + 6.08%). The beta 1.34 is Damodaran's global electrical-equipment figure, a provisional stand-in (his emerging-markets file couldn't be opened and no local 5-year beta was found). It is high for a CSE share and is the single biggest reason fair value is far below the price. WACC 21.3% (debt 4% of capital).

**Methods (bear / base / bull, Rs a share).**
- Sum of the parts: 37.10 / 46.23 / 55.89. DCF of the operating business from after-tax operating profit Rs 5.0 / 5.9 / 5.9bn, growth 4% / 8% / 11% for five years then 4% / 5% / 6%, return on new capital 12% / 16% / 20%, less net debt Rs 3.0bn; plus Rs 15.49 of investments less minorities.
- P/E: 27.84 / 37.79 / 49.72. EPS to March 2027 Rs 7.60 / 9.10 / 10.30 × justified P/E 3.7 / 4.2 / 4.8.
- Justified P/B: 28.44 / 39.15 / 53.55. ROE 14% / 17% / 20%.
- Residual income: 17.53 / 28.67 / 47.69.
Weighted 30/50/20: Rs 27.73 / 37.96 / 51.71 → fair value Rs 37.64; buy Rs 31.99 (−15%), strong buy Rs 28.23 (−25%).

**Growth and reinvestment.** 2025/26 reinvestment was Rs 4.37bn, almost all stock and receivables as copper prices rose; capex Rs 0.40bn against Rs 0.37bn of depreciation, no growth project named, and the report says it was mainly debt-funded. Supported growth 14.5% (68.8% reinvested × 21.1% return on capital); the assumed 4% / 8% / 11% are all within it. Base EPS Rs 9.10 equals the Rs 9.13 run-rate.

**Business tests.** Returns pass (17.8% twelve-month ROE); debt passes (net cash Rs 10.4bn with investments); steady profit passes (no loss in ten years, but copper-driven swings); cash fails (operating cash minus Rs 4.66bn in six months, payout 7%).

**Management and owners.** Management calls 2025/26 its best year ever and expects to beat it, while warning that copper and the rupee may squeeze margins, which the half-year margin of 24% confirmed. Exports are delivering (+46%). The family's 62.08% is now held entirely by the Managing Director, H.A.S. Madanayake; the EPF rose to 10.00%.

**Buy plan (500 shares).** 200 at up to Rs 37.64, 150 at up to Rs 31.99, 150 at up to Rs 28.23: about Rs 16,561 in total. That needs a fall of about two-thirds from Rs 97.80, well below this year's Rs 81.00–107.75 range, so realistically this is a share to watch.

**What would change the view.** Higher: a lower required return (bond yields, country risk, or a verified local beta well below 1.34), copper staying high without hurting demand, margins back to 27–28%, stock and loans falling. Lower: copper falling, less CEB and construction spending, short-term loans rising further, the rupee strengthening.

**Uncertain.** The beta is provisional. Interest paid isn't shown separately in the interim's cash flow, so twelve-month cash before interest can't be worked out (the DCF uses operating profit instead). The minorities are valued at book, which may understate them.

requiredReturn.betaBasis: Provisional. Damodaran's global Electrical Equipment unlevered beta corrected for cash (1.34, January 2026), used because his emerging-markets dataset couldn't be opened in this run; not relevered because ACL holds more cash and investments than debt. No local 5-year beta found. Refresh in January 2027.
sources: Mature-market premium 4.2% and volatility factor 1.52: Damodaran, Country Risk, July 2026
Cost of debt: interest paid Rs 0.128bn ÷ average borrowings and leases Rs 1.80bn (Annual Report 2025/26, pp. 122, 125)
Weights: market cap Rs 70.3bn at Rs 97.80 (CSE close 20 Nov 2026), net debt Rs 3.0bn (30 Sep 2026)
requiredReturn.note: Cost of equity = 8.24% + 1.34 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 22.0%; bear +1.5, bull −1.5 points. WACC weights equity 95.9% and after-tax debt (7.11% × (1 − 30.8%) = 4.9%) 4.1%. The cost of debt is below the house range (bond − 4 points) because the loans are short-term, AWPLR-linked bank lines; at a 4% weight it barely matters.

dcf.addOnNote: Investments the DCF leaves out, less minorities, at 30 Sep 2026 book values: unit trusts Rs 6.229bn + deposits Rs 7.193bn + investment property Rs 2.529bn + associates Rs 0.853bn + FVOCI shares Rs 0.858bn − non-controlling interests Rs 6.526bn = Rs 11.136bn ÷ 718.72mn shares = Rs 15.49 a share.

valuation.note: Fair value weights the bear/base/bull averages of four methods (sum of the parts built on a whole-company DCF, P/E, justified P/B, residual income) 30/50/20: Rs 27.73 / 37.96 / 51.71, giving Rs 37.64 (0.68x NAV). All four come from scripts/valuation.py. Down from Rs 39.10 because residual income now holds the 8% payout for all ten years and minorities are subtracted at book value rather than as a hand-applied 86% share.

management.source: Annual Report 2025/26: Chairman's message (pp. 36–37), Managing Director's report (pp. 38–39), management discussion and analysis (pp. 12–21), manufactured capital (p. 29); progress from the interim to 30 September 2026
management.takeaway: Management calls 2025/26 the best year in the company's history and expects to beat it, but its own outlook warns that dearer copper and a weaker rupee may squeeze margins, and that is what the first half of 2026/27 showed.

said.text: Group revenue rose 21% to Rs 45.5bn and profit after tax to a record Rs 7.3bn, on the restart of construction and record CEB cable orders
Plants ran at peak capacity through the year
Copper and aluminium prices have risen sharply with the Middle East conflict and the rupee has weakened; if sustained these will compress margins unless prices rise
Weaknesses named: dependence on the local construction market and on a few public-sector buyers
Capex of Rs 400mn in 2025/26 was mainly funded by debt; borrowings rose 57% to Rs 2.18bn

plans.text: Expand exports (now sold to more than 10 countries) and open new regions to reduce reliance on the local market
Win a larger share of the institutional (project) market with new products
Grow retail share, pushing its switch and MCB ranges
Manage the input-cost squeeze through pricing, supply-chain changes, cost control and possible currency hedging

investing.text: Keep directing investment to value-added and export-oriented products; no project or amount named
No material capital commitments at 31 March 2026

track.promise: Grow and surpass the record 2025/26 year
track.result: Six-month revenue up 22% and profit to owners up 7%, but the September quarter's EPS was Rs 2.04 against Rs 2.06
Export sales Rs 6.23bn in six months, up 46% from Rs 4.27bn, now 24% of revenue

track.promise: Protect margins against higher copper prices and a weaker rupee
track.result: Gross margin 24.0% in the half (28.0% a year earlier); 23.8% in the September quarter

track.promise: Keep a strong balance sheet (gearing 5.07% at March 2026)
